note: Declares parallax factors for the four plated styles, so their depth stacks deliver motion rather than only separation. No style's appearance at rest changes: parallax is zero-offset by construction and every factor sits behind a prefers-reduced-motion guard.
retune_reasons: Parallax is a fraction of the viewport's travel, and the DEPTH IMPRESSION COMES FROM THE SPREAD rather than from any single factor. Two plates at 0.20 and 0.22 read as one flat picture that lags; the same two at 0.04 and 0.46 read as a foreground moving past a distance. Every set below is chosen for its spread first and its absolute values second.

engraved-colonnade-vector: distance 0.04, arcade 0.22, canopy 0.46. The arcade is the subject and sits at the middle rate; the sea and horizon behind it barely move, which is what makes the columns appear to pass; the leaf canopy overhead moves most because it is nearest the viewer. It also sways — 26s at 0.006 of the short edge — because leaves move and stone does not, and an ambient loop on the wrong layer is the fastest way to make a still subject look unstable.

survey-relief: paper 0.0, contours 0.10, survey 0.20. A survey plate is a document, and a document does not have deep space — the paper is literally pinned, and the contour and furniture layers lift barely off it. The whole spread is 0.20 against the colonnade's 0.42, which is the difference between a scene and a sheet.

pale-moon: void 0.02, burst 0.08, orb 0.16. A celestial subject is far away by definition, so the spread is the smallest in the catalog: everything is nearly at infinity and moves nearly together. The burst breathes at 32s and 0.012 amplitude, which is light doing what light does; the orb itself does not, because a moon that pulsed would read as an error rather than as atmosphere.

tidal-halftone: paper 0.0, sky 0.07, headland 0.28. The headland is the near mass and drifts at 40s and 0.004 — the slowest and smallest loop in the catalog, because it is standing in for a tide, and a tide a reader can see moving is a wave.

No ambient loop runs faster than 26s or wider than 0.012 of the short edge. The catalog's floor is 8s and its ceiling 0.05, and every style sits far inside both: an ambient motion a reader can time reads as a distraction, and one they can measure against the frame reads as a wobble. These are meant to be noticed only in their absence.

Nothing here changes what a style looks like at rest. Parallax resolves to zero with no scroll offset, every transform sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and the flat composite stays the default deliverable — so a consumer that ignores the manifest, and a viewer who asks for reduced motion, both get exactly the picture the catalog shipped before this version.

Every style's version is incremented so an install that already holds these rows takes the new value. The seed upserts on id and replaces the row, so a version that does not bump is indistinguishable from one that was never applied.
